//exclude: 🔴 There is no `exclude`, deliberately. It read `["src/**/*.test.ts"]`, and the root
tsconfig covers only `src/`, `bin/` and `examples/` — so this workspace's 24 test files were
type-checked by nothing at all. `node --test` runs them by stripping types, never by checking
them, so a broken type import runs perfectly.
That is the same hole the root tsconfig's own `//include` note describes for `examples/`: a
file that shipped a real TS2741 while every gate stayed green. It was closed there and left
open here. `packages/manager` never had it — its `include` is `src/**/*.ts`, tests and all.
Turning the check on found two real errors immediately: a `type SiteHost` imported from a
module that does not re-export it, and `unapproved: 0` where the type is an array.
Written as a `//`-prefixed key rather than a `//` comment because `src/web-check-gate.test.ts`
reads this file with `JSON.parse`, which is not JSONC. The root tsconfig uses the same trick.
